jobs.description: The University Hospital Essen offers first class medical services in the Ruhr metropolis. Patient care is connected with basic and translational research at an internationally competitive level.Hemoglobin is best known for its role in oxygen transport in red blood cells. GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The Research Unit Magmatic and Hydrothermal Systems (MuHS) of the research division 4 - Dynamics of the Ocean Floor is offering a position preferably starting as soon as possible. The position offers the possibility to attain a doctoral degree in natural sciences.The position is within the framework of the project “Understanding Core-Mantle Interaction Through Global Mapping of Ultra-Low Velocity Zones in Mantle Convection Models”, which is part of the German Science Foundation's Priority Programm SPP 2404 DeepDyn (https://www.geo.lmu.de/deepdyn/en/) about reconstructing the deep dynamics of planet Earth over geologic time.Ultra-Low Velocity Zones (ULVZs) are thin patches at the base of Earth’s mantle-only tens of kilometres high yet 100 to 1000 km wide-where seismic shear waves exhibit extreme reductions of 20-30%. They are archives of Earth’s thermochemical evolution, potentially reflecting its early differentiation or interactions with the core, but also more recent mantle flow patterns. Yet these interpretations depend critically on ULVZ composition, which remains poorly constrained.The doctoral researcher will numerically model ULVZ evolution and properties in plate-guided global mantle convection simulations. They will develop a framework that quantitatively evaluates these simulations by inferring ULVZ properties from mineral physics and comparing them to seismic constraints, including ULVZ geometry, geographic location and distribution. They will synthesize these results to deliver the first global ULVZ map based on dynamic simulations and to discriminate among proposed ULVZ compositions. The work will be performed as part of SPP 2404 DeepDyn with numerous opportunities for collaboration with national and international partners and other doctoral researchers.Development and analysis of numerical geodynamic models that include ULVZsUse of mineral physics modeling tools to compute properties of lower mantle materialsConducting a parameter study with varying ULVZ and lowermost mantle propertiesDevelopment of a probabilistic framework to assess models using seismic observationsAnalysis of the best-fitting simulations in terms of links between ULVZs and plume formation as well as core-mantle boundary heat flux and topographyContribution of relevant software implementations to open-source research softwareCollaboration with international partners who are experts on mineral physics modeling software and seismic observationsPresentation of relevant results at national and international scientific conferences and publication in scientific journalsMaster´s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field (e.g. geophysics, physics, mathematics, planetary sciences or a related field)Fluency written and spoken English languageExperience with numerical modeling or model analysisProgramming experience (preferably C++)Strong background in the dynamics of Earth’s interior, fluid dynamics, or a closely related area (demonstrated through relevant coursework, research experience, or equivalent training)The following are also desirableExperience in the development, analysis and interpretation of geodynamic modelsExperience with the geodynamic modeling software ASPECT or other geodynamic modeling software, ideally including personal contributions to software developmentExperience with quantitative methods for model assessment, statistical inference, or uncertainty quantificationExperience with mineral physics computations (e.g., using...Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The research group Plankton Imaging Technology and Deep-Sea Zooplankton Ecology at GEOMAR (in cooperation with Kiel University’s Marine Data Science Group) is offering a position in the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” starting at the earliest possible date.The position is offered for a duration of 3 years, with the possibility of extension. In the first year, the successful candidate will be employed by GEOMAR at 75%, supplemented by a 25% contract at Kiel University. Years two and three are fully funded at 100% (pay grade E13 according to the collective agreement for the public sector, TVöD, depending on experience).The position offers the opportunity to pursue a doctoral degree in natural or computer science as a member of the “Helmholtz School for Marine Data Science” (MarDATA). MarDATA’s interdisciplinary focus spans supercomputing, modeling, (bio)informatics, robotics, statistics, and big data methodologies. Doctoral researchers benefit from a structured training program that promotes cross-disciplinary collaboration and provides in-depth scientific insight as well as a systematic approach to marine data science. For more information, visit: https://www.mardata.de/. As part of the MarDATA doctoral network, the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” aims at exploring the use of underwater light field cameras for observing and characterizing plankton organisms (zooplankton) in the ocean. Light field cameras deviate from off-the-shelf cameras in that all rays have to pass through an extra microlens array that changes their direction. Effectively, this means photographing the object from several slightly different perspectives, allowing focussing or 3D reasoning after image capture. The effects intertwine with refraction at the underwater housing and light-medium interaction in front of the camera.The successful applicant willcombine mathematical models for light field cameras and physical principles of refraction and underwater light propagation in order to simulate the image formation processemploy and extend methods of inverse rendering to visually reconstruct plankton from light field imagesdevelop workflows to extract ecological variables from light field imageryinvestigate, how automated classification can be improved by the extra 3D or raw information contained in light field imagesdevelop techniques for geometric co-calibration of light field images with a bioluminescence-sensitive camera in order to create 3D plankton models of bioluminescent deep-sea organismsIt is also expected that the successful applicant will create and contribute to creation and presentation of scientific publications, develop software for calibration, simulation and reconstruction, and is willing to perform and support data acquisition in the lab or at sea during scientific research cruises and collaborate with colleagues from other disciplines as well as the marine technology. We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Postdoctoral Fellow in Computational Cancer Evolution (f/m/x)Department I of Internal Medicine - CECADYour tasksWe are looking for an ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a proven track record in computational cancer evolution to join our Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory at the CECAD Research Center in Cologne. In this role, you will reconstruct the clonal and subclonal architecture of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and track its evolution under targeted therapies. Using bulk and single-cell sequencing data, you will infer tumour phylogenies and quantify intratumour heterogeneity, subclonal selection and genomic instability (e.g. copy-number alterations, whole-genome doubling and chromothripsis).You will identify evolutionary trajectories leading to treatment resistance, relapse and Richter transformation. Furthermore, you will develop and apply computational methods based on evolutionary principles and integrate genomic, transcriptomic and spatial data with clinical outcomes. Your analyses will link evolutionary features to treatment response, MRD kinetics and survival.For this work, the lab has access to blood and bone marrow samples from more than 900 patients with CLL treated within prospective clinical trials of the German CLL Study Group (GCLLSG), including samples taken before treatment and at relapse, linked to detailed clinical and measurable residual disease (MRD) data.You will lead your own projects, contribute to collaborative projects within the lab and with external partners, and co-supervise PhD and Master students.Your profile• A PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, statistics, physics, computer science or a related field• A proven track record in computational cancer evolution, demonstrated by first-author publications• Hands-on experience in reconstructing clonal and subclonal tumour evolution from sequencing data (e.g. clonal deconvolution, phylogenetic inference, mutational signatures)• Experience in copy-number and structural variant analysis from whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing data; experience with single-cell DNA or RNA sequencing data is a plus• Fluency in Python and/or R, and experience with reproducible workflows (e.g. Snakemake, Nextflow) on high performance computing clusters• Experience with longitudinal or clinical trial data and with haematological malignancies is a plus• Ability to work independently and in close collaboration with clinicians and wet-lab scientists• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spokenOur offer• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.Your future in detailThe Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory (www.al-sawaf-lab.com), led by Prof Othman Al-Sawaf and based at the CECAD and Department I of Internal Medicine, was founded in 2024 and is funded by a large Emmy-Noether-Grant of the German Research Council (DFG). The focus of the lab is to integrate multimodal analyses to study the plasticity, evolution and prognosis of cancer with a special focus on hematological malignancies. To this end, the lab utilizes a unique biobank with blood and bone marrow samples from patients treated within large (>900 patients) prospective clinical trials. The group is embedded in a network with many local collaborators, including the Collaborative Research Center (CRC) 1530 and the German CLL Study Group (GCLLSG), as well as many national and international partners in academia and industry. Previous work has been frequently cited (Al-Sawaf et al, N Engl J Med 2025; Al-Sawaf et al, Nature Medicine 2024; Al-Sawaf et al, Nature Medicine 2023; see Pubmed) and the aim of the lab is to continue producing highly impactful and patient-relevant results.ContactProf. Dr. Othman Al-SawafTel: +49 221 478-84816Universitätsklinikum Köln AöRGeschäftsbereich PersonalKerpener Str. 6250937 KölnUniklinik Köln Karriere Application deadline: 29 November 2026Job-ID: 3ftptfctWe look forward to receiving your application and getting to know you!

With a tradition spanning more than 600 years, the Faculty of Medicine at Leipzig University is one of the largest research institutions in the Leipzig region. With more than 1.300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and provides training for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine and dentistry as well as pharmacy and midwifery. The Faculty of Medicine was founded in 1415, making it one of the oldest medical faculties in Germany with an unbroken tradition of teaching.PhD Position - Craniofacial Biology and PTEN-Dependent Tissue HomeostasisThe research group "Cranio- and Orofacial Development" (https://research.uni-leipzig.de/petersen_lab/) at Leipzig University Medical Center (UKL) offers a PhD position within a DFG-funded collaborative project investigating PTEN-dependent craniofacial tissue homeostasis. The project is particularly suited to candidates interested in craniofacial and skeletal biology, molecular signaling, spatial omics, and metabolism.Project BackgroundPTEN is a central regulator of PI3K-AKT signaling and coordinates cell growth, metabolism, and tissue homeostasis. The project investigates how loss of PTEN in the osteoblast lineage alters the postnatal craniofacial complex. The PhD project will focus on teeth and their supporting periodontal tissues, alveolar and craniofacial bone, and the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). Using an inducible postnatal genetic mouse model, we aim to determine how PTEN-dependent signaling changes tissue architecture, bone remodeling, cellular states, and molecular programs. A complementary part of the project will investigate the associated adipose/metabolic phenotype in close collaboration with Dr. Antje Garten and her group from the Molecular Endocrinology at the Center for Pediatric Research (https://research.uni-leipzig.de/garten_lab/).The PhD candidate will investigate- PTEN-dependent changes in teeth and periodontal tissues, craniofacial and alveolar bone, and the TMJ- Cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying altered bone remodeling and craniofacial tissue homeostasis after postnatal PTEN deletion- Spatially resolved tissue responses and their relationship to PTEN-associated adipose/metabolic changesMethods and ApproachesThe project combines state-of-the-art experimental and computational techniques, including:- Inducible transgenic mouse models and genetic reporter systems- Histology, immunofluorescence, advanced microscopy, and micro-computed tomography- Spatial transcriptomics of dental, periodontal, bone, and TMJ tissues- Molecular biology, quantitative image analysis, proteomic integration, and bioinformatic analysesCandidate ProfileWe are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:- Master of Science degree or a Diploma in Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Bioinformatics or Chemistry- Interest in craniofacial biology, mechanobiology, or regenerative medicine- Experience in molecular biology, cell biology, animal models, and/or bioinformatics- Strong motivation to work in an international and interdisciplinary research environment- Good communication skills and proficiency in EnglishResearch EnvironmentThe project is embedded in the Department of Orthodontics at Leipzig University Medical Center. Our research focuses on craniofacial biology, tooth and periodontal tissue homeostasis, skeletal remodeling, genetic mouse models, advanced imaging, and spatial omics. The collaboration with Dr. Antje Garten provides complementary expertise in PTEN biology, metabolism, and adipose tissue, enabling the PhD candidate to connect local craniofacial phenotypes with systemic metabolic alterations.Institution: Department für Kopf- und Zahnmedizin, Poliklinik für KieferorthopädieType of employment: Fixed-term position for 3 years (third-party funded)Working Hours: part-time (26,00h)Start date: 01.12.2026Remuneration: TV-L 13- A fully funded PhD position (3 years)- Participation in an international research collaboration- Access to cutting-edge technologies, including spatial transcriptomics and advanced imaging- A dynamic and collaborative research environment- Opportunities for international exchange and conference participationHow to applyPlease apply with a single PDF containing a cover letter describing your previous research experience and motivation to join our lab; curriculum vitae; copies of relevant qualifications (degree, diploma and, if applicable, animal-course certificates); and the contact details of two refereesApply now for this position via our applicant portal by 31 October 2026 .Your contact personFor further information about the application process, please contact Dr. Julian Petersen (E: Julian.Petersen@medizin.uni-leipzig.de).Applicants with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration if equally qualified. Please include relevant supporting documentation with your application.Please note that, due to legal requirements, we can only employ applicants who are immune to measles. You will be required to provide the relevant proof of immunity.For information on data protection, please visit: Data protection
